source: High Country Fly Fishing Guides and Locals

conditions.overall: The Watauga River has been fishing excellently with feeder streams adding extra water and fish feeding well. The South Holston is running high with consistent 24/7 dam releases and sulphur hatches occurring during generations.

tactics: On the Watauga, the dam does an hour pulse in the AM, normally from 6–7 AM, followed by normal rec flow beginning at 1 PM — time your fishing accordingly.
Above the Doe on the Watauga, focus on normal summer bugs: small midges, baetis, and scuds.
Below the Doe on the Watauga, target the heavy caddis activity with caddis dries and caddis nymphs.
On the South Holston, watch for sulphur hatches occurring during generation periods.
The South Holston dam is running 24/7 for the foreseeable future — always check current TVA release schedules before heading out, as flows can change without notice.
No stocking will occur in any delayed harvest streams in WNC until October — fish only wild streams in the area for now.

waters.name: Watauga River (East Tennessee)
waters.note: Fishing has been excellent. Feeder streams Doe and Stoney Creek have been pumping in extra water for at least a month, keeping fish happy and feeding well. Dam does an hour pulse AM from 6–7 AM, then normal rec flow from 1 PM.

waters.name: Doe Creek
waters.note: Feeder stream to the Watauga — has been pumping in extra water for at least a month.

waters.name: Stoney Creek
waters.note: Feeder stream to the Watauga — has been pumping in extra water for at least a month.

waters.name: South Holston (East Tennessee)
waters.note: With Holston Lake nearing full pool, more generations have started. Sulphur hatches occurring during generations. Dam is running 24/7 for the foreseeable future. High water conditions after a long stretch without consistent releases.

elevation_note: High Country streams (Boone, 3300-4000ft) run 1-2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC
stocking_note: No stocking will occur in any delayed harvest streams in WNC until October.
